target.title: fix: allow configuring Slack App Home copy
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack App Home currently publishes fixed OpenClaw copy even when an installation configures a different app-facing name or slash command. That can make the Home tab inconsistent with the workspace's configured Slack app presentation and command path.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a Slack `appHome` config block at the root and per-account levels so operators can customize the safe Home tab title, description, and footer, or disable Home tab publishing entirely. The default behavior remains unchanged for existing installs, and the fallback usage line now reflects the configured `slashCommand.name` when no custom description is provided.

## User Impact

Slack operators can make the App Home tab match their configured app name and slash command, such as `Acme Corp Assistant` with `/acme`, without forking the Slack plugin. Existing installations keep the current OpenClaw Home tab copy unless they opt into the new config.

## Evidence

The source behavior on `main` builds the Slack Home view with a fixed `OpenClaw` title and `/openclaw` usage text while Slack `slashCommand.name` is configurable. This PR moves that copy behind configuration and keeps the default copy unchanged when no override is set.

Focused validation:

```text
pnpm test -- extensions/slack/src/monitor/events/home.test.ts extensions/slack/src/config-schema.test.ts
✓ extensions/slack/src/monitor/events/home.test.ts (6 tests)
✓ extensions/slack/src/config-schema.test.ts (25 tests)
Test Files 2 passed; Tests 31 passed
```

Additional checks:

```text
pnpm docs:list
pnpm exec oxfmt --check docs/channels/slack.md extensions/slack/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/slack/src/monitor/events/home.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Known local proof gap: full local lint/build was not run. The local worktree did not have its own `node_modules`; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is currently blocked by an existing patchedDependencies lockfile mismatch, and the lint wrapper then failed while preparing plugin-SDK boundary artifacts because `markdown-it-cjk-friendly` could not be resolved from the borrowed modules dir.
